transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling Cymbal Telecom Business Support. My name is Sarah. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Hello Sarah. My name is Michael Brown, I'm with the accounting department at Delta Legal Services. I'm calling about our most recent bill. It seems to be incorrect.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly help you with that, Michael. I just need to verify the account for security purposes. Could you please provide me with the account's Customer ID?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, of course. The customer ID is CUST-2013.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. That's CUST-2013. And for the final verification step, could you please provide the 6-digit security PIN associated with the account?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Let me see... yes, the PIN is 1-2-7-2-7-4.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Perfect, thank you for verifying that. I have the account for Delta Legal Services pulled up here. You mentioned there was an issue with the latest bill?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That's right. For the past year, our bill has been a consistent amount, but this new invoice is about twenty dollars higher. Nothing has changed on our end, so I need to understand why the price went up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand completely. Unexpected bill increases are no fun. Let me just open the most recent invoice and compare it to the previous one. This will just take a moment.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Please do. I have them both in front of me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, I'm seeing it now. I see the invoice from last month, and the total was, let's see... three hundred and twenty-nine dollars, before taxes.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Correct. And this month's is three hundred forty-nine dollars before taxes. A twenty dollar difference.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, that's exactly what I'm seeing on my end as well. Please allow me another moment to examine the line items on the account to see what caused that change.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, thank you for your patience, Michael. I've found the reason for the change. It looks like when you signed up for the Business Dedicated Fiber 500Mbps plan, it came with a 12-month promotional discount of twenty dollars per month.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: A promotional discount... I see. I assumed that was the standard rate.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's a common point of confusion. The standard rate for the service is $349 per month, and that promotional credit brought it down to $329 for the first year. That 12-month period just ended, so the service has now reverted to its standard monthly rate.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I see. Is that something that was outlined in the original agreement? I'd have to go back and look through our files.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, it would have been. I can see the note on the account from the initial setup. It specifies the 'New Customer Promotional Credit - $20.00 x 12 months'. I can email you a copy of that original service agreement if you'd like.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, that's okay for now. I believe you. It's just... we're a long-standing customer and we rely on predictable expenses. A sudden increase isn't ideal. Is there anything you can do for us? Any other promotions or loyalty discounts available?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand your position, and I want to thank you for your loyalty to Cymbal Telecom. Let me check what offers are currently available for your account. Business accounts often have different options than residential ones. Can I place you on a brief hold for two to three minutes while I check with our retention department's offer list?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, a hold is fine. Thank you, Sarah.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. Please hold.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you so much for your patience, Michael. I've reviewed the available offers for your account.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No problem. What did you find?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay, so I have a couple of possibilities we can explore. The first and most straightforward option is a 'Business Loyalty Credit'. I can apply a ten dollar per month credit to your account for the next 12 months.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So, that would make the bill three hundred thirty-nine dollars a month, instead of three forty-nine?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's correct. It's not the full twenty dollars, but it's a ten dollar savings each month.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Hmm. Okay. And does that require a new contract or extending our current one?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a great question. No, this particular credit does not require any contract extension. It's simply a thank you for your business.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay. What was the other option you mentioned?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The other option is a bit different. We have a promotion right now for businesses to upgrade their service tier. I see you're on the 500 Megabit per second plan.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, that's what we have.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We could upgrade you to our Business Dedicated Fiber 1 Gigabyte plan. That's double your current speed.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: And what would the cost for that be? I imagine it's more expensive.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Normally, yes. The standard rate for the 1 Gig plan is $399 per month. However, there's a promotion that would give you a sixty dollar per month credit if you sign a new 24-month agreement.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So let me get this straight. The price would be three hundred and thirty-nine dollars a month? For double the speed?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, that's exactly right. Three hundred and ninety-nine minus sixty. So, the monthly rate would be the same as the first option, three hundred and thirty-nine dollars, but you'd get the upgraded 1 Gig service.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: But that would require a new two-year contract.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Correct. A new 24-month term would start from the day of the upgrade.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: And what happens after those 24 months? Does the price jump to $399?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, after the 24-month promotional period ends, the service would revert to the standard rate for the 1 Gig plan at that time.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I see. I'm not authorized to sign a new two-year contract on the spot. That would require discussion with the partners here.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand. It's a significant commitment.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Let's go back to that first option. The ten dollar credit. You said that was for 12 months?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, 12 months, with no contract extension.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: And after 12 months, the price goes back to $349?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is correct. We could, of course, have this same conversation again in a year to see what new loyalty offers are available then.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay. That seems like the most prudent option for now. It doesn't lock us into anything.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It certainly offers the most flexibility.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Is there... any chance that credit could be a little higher? Maybe fifteen dollars? To split the difference of the original twenty?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a fair question, Michael. The system automatically generates these offers based on account tenure and service type. Ten dollars is what it presented me.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So there's no way to adjust it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well... let me try something. Sometimes, there's a little leeway for long-term business accounts. Would you mind holding for just another minute or two? I want to see if I can get a supervisor to approve a slightly higher credit.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Oh, yes, I would appreciate that very much. Thank you for being willing to try.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Of course. I want to make sure we're doing everything we can. Please hold.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Michael? Thank you again for holding. I appreciate your patience.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Not a problem. Any luck?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I have some good news. I spoke with my supervisor, and given that Delta Legal Services has been a Cymbal Telecom customer for over five years with a perfect payment history, we were able to get an exception approved.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That's great to hear.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We can apply a 'Valued Business Partner' credit of fifteen dollars per month for the next 12 months.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Fifteen dollars! That's excellent. Thank you, Sarah. I really appreciate you going the extra mile on that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's my pleasure. We value your business. So, to confirm, you'd like me to apply the fifteen-dollar monthly credit for 12 months, with no contract extension?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, that's exactly what I'd like. Please proceed.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. I'm adding the credit to your account right now. Just a few clicks... and... okay. It is now active.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So, what does this mean for the current bill? The one that's for $349?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is an excellent question. Since this billing cycle has already been generated, the invoice itself won't change. You will still need to pay the $349 plus tax for this current bill.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Oh. I see.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: However, the fifteen dollar credit has been applied to the account starting today. This means on your next bill, you will see a credit for the pro-rated portion of this month, and the full fifteen dollar credit for the next billing cycle.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Can you explain that a bit more clearly? What will my next bill look like?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Certainly. Let's look at the calendar. Your billing cycle runs from the 5th to the 4th of each month. We're about halfway through this cycle.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, yes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So for this current cycle, you'll get a credit for roughly half a month. A fifteen dollar credit for a full month is about fifty cents a day. So you'll get a pro-rated credit of approximately seven dollars and fifty cents on the next bill to cover the second half of this month.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay, a pro-rated credit. Got it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Then, for the next full billing period, you'll see the full fifteen dollar credit. So your next invoice will show the standard $349 charge, then a line item for the $7.50 pro-rated credit, and another line item for the $15.00 monthly credit.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: So the total due, before taxes, will be three hundred forty-nine, minus seven-fifty, minus fifteen... which is... three hundred twenty-six dollars and fifty cents?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's exactly right. Your next bill will be for $326.50 plus taxes.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: And the bill after that?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The bill after that, and for the following ten months, will be for the standard charge of $349 minus the $15 credit. So, it will be $334 plus tax.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Okay. $334. That's a number I can work with. Thank you for clarifying all of that. It can get a bit confusing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not at all, I'm happy to break it down. It's important that you understand exactly what to expect on your invoices.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: I agree. Can you send me an email confirming this change? Just something I can attach to my internal report on this.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Absolutely. I am composing an email to you right now. I have the contact email on file as michael.brown@deltalegalservices.com. Is that still the correct address?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Yes, that's correct.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great. The email will summarize our conversation, confirm the application of the $15 'Valued Business Partner' credit for 12 months, and state the new effective monthly rate of $334 plus tax. I'll also add a reference number for this call. Is there anything else you'd like me to include?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, that sounds perfect. That's everything I need.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay... and... sent. You should receive that email within the next five to ten minutes. It will be coming from a Cymbal Telecom support address.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Excellent. I'll keep an eye out for it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So, to recap, we've identified the reason for the bill increase was an expiring promotion, and we've applied a new $15 monthly credit for the next 12 months to bring the cost down.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: That's right. You've been very helpful, Sarah.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure to assist you, Michael.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: The service itself has always been solid, we've never had an outage with your dedicated fiber. It's good to know the customer service is just as reliable.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I love to hear that. We pride ourselves on the reliability of our network and our support team. The 'SLA Guarantees' on your business plan mean we take that very seriously.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: It shows. Well, that's all I needed today. You've resolved my issue completely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wonderful. Was there anything else at all I could help you with? Any other questions about your Cymbal Telecom services?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: No, that's it for me. Thank you again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are very welcome. Thank you for calling Cymbal Telecom Business Support, and we appreciate you being a valued customer. Have a wonderful rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: You too, Sarah. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Oh, wait, Sarah, are you still there?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I'm still here, Michael. Is everything okay?

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Sorry, one last quick question just popped into my head. The email you sent, will it have a reference number for our call today?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, it will. I included a call interaction ID in the body of the email for your records. It will be clearly labeled.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: Perfect, perfect. Sorry to keep you. That's really all now. Thanks again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It is absolutely no problem at all. I'm glad you asked to make sure you have everything you need. Have a great afternoon.

transcript.speaker: User
transcript.text: You too. Bye now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bye.
